text: Young Sheldon is an American sitcom created by Chuck Lorre and Steven Molaro that aired on CBS from September 25, 2017, to May 16, 2024. It is a spin-off prequel to The Big Bang Theory, set from the late 1980s to the mid-1990s and centered on the childhood of Sheldon Cooper, a gifted prodigy growing up with his family in Medford, Texas. The series stars Iain Armitage as Sheldon, alongside Zoe Perry, Lance Barber, Montana Jordan, Raegan Revord, and Annie Potts. Jim Parsons, who portrayed adult Sheldon on The Big Bang Theory, serves as the series' narrator and an executive producer. Development began in November 2016, when Parsons shared an initial idea with The Big Bang Theory producers, and the series was ordered by CBS in March 2017 after Armitage and Perry were cast. It premiered as a special preview on September 25, 2017, and began airing weekly on November 2, 2017. CBS announced in November 2023 that the series would end after its seventh season, with the one-hour finale airing on May 16, 2024. The show received positive reviews from critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 76% approval rating and Metacritic assigning a 63 out of 100 score indicating generally favorable reviews. The series opens in fall 1989 with nine-year-old Sheldon beginning high school at Medford High School; as a child prodigy, he excels academically but struggles socially. His mother, Mary, often clashes with his scientific skepticism, while his father, George Sr., tries to understand him despite their differences. Sheldon shares a competitive yet close bond with his twin sister Missy and feels overshadowed by Sheldon’s achievements, while his older brother Georgie matures into his late teens and eventually drops out of high school at age seventeen to work full-time, demonstrating his sales skills. Sheldon begins auditing physics classes taught by Dr. John Sturgis at East Texas Tech College, and his grandmother Constance (Meemaw), who calls him "Moonpie," supports him and begins a romantic relationship with Dr. Sturgis. The family faces financial difficulties and George Sr.’s demanding coaching schedule. Sheldon forms a friendship with Tam Nguyen, a Vietnamese-American classmate who introduces him to comic books and Dungeons & Dragons, and meets Paige Swanson, another child prodigy who becomes both a friend and academic rival. Sheldon graduates high school at age eleven as valedictorian in fall 1991 and begins full-time college at East Texas Tech. Dr. Sturgis experiences a mental health crisis that disrupts Sheldon’s academic progress and strains his relationship with Meemaw. George Sr. faces increasing pressure as head football coach and deals with marital tensions with Mary, who becomes attracted to a younger pastor named Pastor Rob. Georgie meets Mandy McAllister, who is about 12 years older than him; both lie about being twenty-one, with Mandy stating she was twenty-five (though she was actually twenty-nine) and Georgie at seventeen. Their relationship becomes serious, and when Mandy becomes pregnant, they get married and have a daughter named Constance, nicknamed "CeeCee" after Meemaw. In the final seasons, George Sr.’s health deteriorates, and after a tornado forces the family to live together, he receives an offer for a prestigious coaching position at Rice University in Houston. Before accepting, he suffers a fatal heart attack during a work-related incident in season seven, episode twelve, leaving Mary, Meemaw, and the children to cope with the loss. The series concludes with Sheldon being accepted into the California Institute of Technology for graduate studies at age fourteen and making the decision to leave Texas to pursue his scientific career. In the finale, adult Sheldon composes his childhood memoir and reflects on his past, with on-screen appearances from his wife Amy and allusions to their children, providing closure to his formative years and connecting to his future in The Big Bang Theory. In January 2024, a spin-off focused on Georgie and Mandy, titled Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage, was announced and greenlit by CBS, with its first episode airing on October 17, 2024. The show’s title sequence features Steve Burns’ "Mighty Little Man," initially showing Sheldon walking out in a bow tie, checked shirt, shorts, and cowboy boots, noticing a cow, and backing away, with variations including a tumbleweed or a black bull in later seasons. From season three onward, the sequence includes the entire Cooper family and Sheldon in various costumes, such as Einstein, Mr. Spock, The Flash, an astronaut, and a train engineer. In season seven, Mandy and Constance (CeeCee) are included, and Georgie shoos the bull away instead of walking back. Reruns aired on Nick at Nite (2020–2022) and CMT (2023–2024), and the series entered syndication in local markets on September 27, 2021, with off-network airing on TBS. Seasons 1–4 were released on HBO Max in 2020, with season 6 added in September 2023. Netflix acquired streaming rights in Australia, Canada, and the UK in October and November 2021, and the first four seasons were added to Netflix in the U.S. on November 24, 2023. The series was unexpectedly added to Disney+ in Australia and New Zealand with all seasons. The first season was released on DVD and Blu-ray on September 4, 2018, followed by subsequent seasons on DVD and Blu-ray through Warner Bros. Home Entertainment and Warner Archive Collection. The seventh and final season was released on DVD on September 24, 2024, with a complete series set, and individual sets of seasons six and seven were released on Blu-ray on the same day. In the UK, the show airs on E4, with season premieres in February 2018 through July 2024. In Israel, it airs on Yes Comedy, and in Southeast Asia, it premiered on Warner TV Asia, with reruns scheduled for April 6, 2025. The show also features guest appearances by Bob Newhart as Professor Proton (younger), Elon Musk as himself in the sixth episode of season one, and other actors like Kaley Cuoco (uncredited voice) and Barber (in different roles) appearing in both series. In the second-season finale, references to The Big Bang Theory’s finale are made, including Sheldon promising to mention his father in his Nobel Prize speech, which he does, and a montage of the main characters as children, with Christine Baranski and Carol Ann Susi making voice appearances. In the finale, adult Sheldon and Amy make their only on-camera appearance together in a future scene in Pasadena, California, as neither of their children had been born when The Big Bang Theory ended in 2019. Iain Armitage, Lance Barber, and Montana Jordan make a guest appearance in The Big Bang Theory via a VHS tape played decades earlier.

iewire described the initial season as “surprising for all the right reasons.” Entertainment Weekly praised the show for “brilliant casting” and called it overall “inoffensive” and “comforting,” noting that compared to The Big Bang Theory, “the companion series don’t share much DNA.” A USA Today review by Kelly Lawler observed that the “changes in style and format may be jarring to regular Big Bang viewers” but credited the show for “not forcing the Big Bang model onto a series where it wouldn’t fit,” and noted that Armitage’s portrayal of Sheldon Cooper is “cute but not cloying, and just blunt and annoying enough to see hints of Parsons’ version of the character nearly three decades older.” Similarly, a Los Angeles Times review stated that the first season “has its own gentler, more naturalistic rhythms and pleasures” compared to its predecessor and that Armitage’s performance is “charming and believable and just suggestive enough of Parsons.” The Colorado Springs Gazette claimed the show is a "smarter, more humorous and heartfelt show" than The Big Bang Theory. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, reviewing only the pilot, called Perry’s performance “a standout” and described the episode as “warm and embraceable but not yet essential viewing.” Vox gave the show two and a half stars, stating, “It’s less of a blatant cash grab than it seems,” but criticized the humor and set design, asserting “it looks a little cheap, relative to the other, glossier single-camera comedies in its rough weight class.” Margaret Lyons of The New York Times argued that the show “isn’t funny” and that “its punch lines… only come from Sheldon’s inappropriate responses.” Noel Murray, reviewing the final season in The Daily Beast, described the show as “charmingly unassuming” and that it “works in softer, mellower tones,” noting that “the comedy often relies on characters hitting the same note over and over” and that “the show isn’t top-shelf, can’t-miss great,” yet affirmed it “connects with a large audience yet still has a meaningful point of view.” The fourth season was one of 101 out of the 200 most-popular scripted television series that received the ReFrame Stamp for the years 2020 to 2021. The stamp, awarded by the gender equity coalition ReFrame and industry database IMDbPro, recognizes film and television projects with gender-balanced hiring, specifically those that hire female-identifying people, especially women of color, in four out of eight key roles for their production. The first and last shots of the series were set to Dire Straits' "Walk of Life." The show features popular Country, Rock, and Pop songs from the 1980s and early 1990s, and occasionally earlier. In January 2024, it was announced that a spin-off series of Young Sheldon, focusing on Georgie Cooper (portrayed by Montana Jordan) and Mandy McAllister (portrayed by Emily Osment), titled Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage, was in development. On March 5, 2024, CBS announced that the series had been ordered. The series premiered on October 17, 2024.
